analysis: Examined EngineV2RequestUsageSignal.swift (base/head) and the MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift patch. Usage signal: the rename _firstWithheldReasoningAt to _firstWithheldOutputAt and the new recordWithheldOutput() only set a lock-guarded timestamp. They store no prompt text and add no logging or telemetry, so A-001 confidentiality is unaffected. withheldReasoning plaintext stays request-local as before. Lock use matches the existing pattern, with no new waiters or continuation changes. The prefix-cache lookup/tier/receipt logic (T-041 area) is unchanged. Scheduler: the patch adds a GLM-only withholding path. (1) GLM media with a withheld JSON answer or forced tool call is now rejected with invalidToolPayload after releaseBox.fire(), before any vision work. This is fail-closed and releases the reservation. (2) emit() buffers GLM JSON answers through GLM5NextResponseFormatOutput.withholding and yields the validated answer only at completion via validatedAnswer(finishReason:). Failure paths call releaseBox.fire() and finish with an error, as the existing formatOutput path does. This is integrity-positive: invalid output is not streamed. (3) nativeReasoningPrefix is now also set when withholdsGLMOutput is true. This only affects reasoning routing. Unverified contracts: GLM5NextPromptPolicy.withholdsOutput, GLM5NextResponseFormatOutput and the router.visibleEvent behavior are outside the supplied source. Also unverified are the callers of the renamed firstWithheldReasoningAt, which are not shown. A missed rename would be a compile error, not a security issue. Possible availability considerations, such as unbounded buffering of withheld answers, are bounded by max_tokens and not evidenced as a regression. No changes to the coordinator/provider boundary, attestation, keys or encryption. No concrete security regression identified. The reviewed patch excerpt is marked incomplete, so some hunks near line 1000 were not fully visible.
